For independent integer exponent columns, different polynomial monomials give distinct Laurent exponents; multiplication by one monomial clears negative powers and preserves nonzero polynomial. Every dependent column becomes algebraic after clearing rational denominators in its column relation. Thus exact transcendence degree equals rational rank, including zero/rank-deficient columns. Positive rational powers are fixed unambiguously, and passing to a common integer power gives an algebraic field extension with the same transcendence degree.

Rank-two/nonsingular-matrix examples correctly give infinite families. Taking r=1/pi is not allowed, and e is not exp(r*pi) for rational nonzero r. The already-established independent pair pi,exp(pi) has dependent pi,log(exp(pi)), correctly disproving arbitrary logarithm transfer. No Schanuel conclusion is imported.
